answer: You can't flip staked funds fast when time locks freeze them. A new identity locks 120 credits for 20 epochs. You get it back only after the lock ends. You can't move it, spend it, or reuse it. The pigment of the lock is visible: everyone sees the funds are frozen. Honest users don't mind, since they earn rewards during the lock. The inlet is narrow by design: 1,000 clones need 120,000 credits locked for 20 epochs. The summit is breakeven at 25 epochs, so an attacker must wait over a month to profit. One proven fake burns the whole 120 credit lock.
